title: Journal-Entry Period Lock Gate
description: Evaluates caller-declared journal entries against a caller-declared, time-varying period-lock policy and reports, per entry, whether the declared policy admits it. Periods carry dated lock events (open, soft_locked with exact-match exempt roles, hard_closed); the lock state is evaluated at the entry's entered_on date (or a declared as_of_date) for the period containing the entry's effective date, which is what makes a detective test possible: an entry entered the day before a soft lock began is admitted even if the period is locked today. Reversal entries resolve under one of three declared ERP conventions (original_date, first_open_period, explicit_date) with the resolved date reported per entry. Per-entry output carries decision (allow / allow_exempt / refuse), period_id, lock_state_at_entry, exempt_role_used, resolved_effective_date, refusal_code, and a self_approval flag comparing caller-declared preparer and approver labels (null when either is absent); totals roll up by decision and by period, and the e

policy_version.description: Caller-declared lock-policy version string; echoed verbatim in the output.

period_id.description: Opaque period label, echoed in per-entry results and totals.

start_date.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, strict calendar (2026-02-29 refuses).

from_date.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD; the state applies on and after this date; must be strictly ascending per period.

state.description: Lock state from this date onward; no event means open.

items.description: Dated lock event; state at D is the last event with from_date <= D.

lock_events.description: Time-varying lock history of the period.

items.description: Declared accounting period with its time-varying lock history.

periods.description: Declared period table; overlapping or inverted periods refuse the whole run.

soft_lock_exempt_roles.description: Roles admitted through a soft lock; exact case-sensitive match, no hierarchy; applies to soft_locked only.

reversal_policy.description: ERP convention used to resolve a reversal entry's effective date. None is required by an accounting standard.

explicit_reversal_date.description: Calendar-valid ISO date; required only when reversal_policy is explicit_date.

as_of_date.description: Preventive-mode fallback: used only for entries that carry no entered_on.

entry_id.description: Opaque synthetic label; echoed, never interpreted.

effective_date.description: Accounting date; determines the period whose lock history applies.

entered_on.description: Entry date: the moment the time-varying lock state is evaluated. Caller-declared, not verified.

roles.description: Roles of the entry; a soft lock admits any exact exempt-role match.

prepared_by.description: Opaque preparer label; compared to approved_by for self_approval.

approved_by.description: Opaque approver label; compared to prepared_by for self_approval.

is_reversal.description: True for reversal entries; the declared reversal policy resolves the effective date.

original_effective_date.description: Reversals: the original entry date being reversed; required unless reversal_policy is explicit_date.

items.description: Declared journal entry. All identity labels are synthetic; zero PII.

entries.description: Declared entries; more than 500 refuses the whole run (ENTRY_CAP_EXCEEDED).

mcp_tool_definition.name: gate_je_period_lock
mcp_tool_definition.description: Evaluates caller-declared journal entries against a caller-declared, time-varying period-lock policy (open, soft_locked with exempt roles, hard_closed) and resolves reversal dates under one of three declared ERP conventions. Per-entry decisions with refusal codes, self-approval flags, totals, and a canonical policy_digest. A bad policy refuses the whole run (did_not_run). Declared facts only: does not prevent posting, does not verify lock history, does not assert fraud or control effectiveness.
